title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-06
source: 7 Inch Half Track Reel Master @ 7.5 ips(Recorded By Bear on a Sony 770 Reel 2 Reel)- 1st Generation Cassettes (TDK SAX-100's) Transferred By Dick Latvala(Master Reel Playback on a Technics 1506 Reel 2 Reel-Tascam 122 MK111 Cassette Deck No Dolby); Analog to Digital Transfer(Cassettes played back on Nakamichi Dragon-Sony PCM-R500 DAT @ 44.1KHz by Jim Wise circa late 1990's) Zero Gen DAT play back on a Sony PCM R-500-Digital Out @ 16/44.1kHz-Digital Audio Labs Card deluxe-WAV @ 16/44.1KHz; Editing(Adobe Audition CC)-Mastering & Processing(iZotope Ozone 6)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name); Jim Wise

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture with reduced hiss and magnificent clarity, showcasing a smoky Alligator jam and tight Dancin' during a relaxed Fillmore West set.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean, low‑hiss soundboard dump that sounds crisp from start to finish, letting the band’s late‑show looseness shine through. After an unremarkable first half, the group rolls into a smoking Alligator jam and a tight Dancin' that highlight why this Fillmore West run feels like a playground for improvisation.

ai_rating.rationale: All reviews praise the performance (especially the second half) and note excellent sound quality with less hiss; the few minor critiques do not outweigh the overall enthusiasm.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Noticeably less hiss than earlier sources, crisp mix, magnificent drumming presence and overall clear, balanced sound throughout.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First half is fairly routine, but the band eases into a relaxed, exploratory vibe at Fillmore West, building momentum with extended jams and tight transitions in the latter portion.

band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ work is highlighted (especially on “The Dew”), adding a distinct texture to the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Superb drumming noted throughout, contributing to the powerful jam sections.
